description: In August 2010, 72 undocumented migrants - 58 men and 14 women, from Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Ecuador and Brazil - were murdered by Los Zetas at a ranch in San Fernando, shot in the back of the head and piled together. It was discovered because one wounded survivor reached a checkpoint on 23 August. The police chief leading the investigation was later killed.
energy_note: Discovered only because one man survived and walked.

description: In March 2011, 193 people were killed at La Joya ranch, taken in hijackings of passenger buses on Federal Highway 101 and buried in 47 clandestine mass graves. The investigation began because luggage went unclaimed in Reynosa and Matamoros. By 7 June 2011, 193 bodies had been recovered.
energy_note: It came to light because suitcases were not collected.

description: Federal prosecutors indicated local police in San Fernando were involved in the 2011 massacres, per a memo from the Attorney General's Office obtained under transparency laws. Detained Zetas reportedly said local police assisted in 'intercepting of people'.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and nothing was published about punishment
description: Amnesty International noted five years on that authorities had made arrests but failed to publish any information as to whether anyone had been sentenced, describing Mexico as becoming a 'no-go zone' for migrants. A year after the 2011 graves, 49 torsos, several believed to be migrants, were found in Cadereyta, Nuevo León.
